newsitem.title: USA: BOXING-DE LA HOYA IS ACHING FOR NEXT WEEK'S FIGHT.
newsitem.headline: BOXING-DE LA HOYA IS ACHING FOR NEXT WEEK'S FIGHT.

text.p: After a six-month layoff, unbeaten World Boxing Council (WBC) super lightweight champion Oscar De La Hoya is aching for next Saturday's title fight against Miguel Angel Gonzalez.

"I feel I haven't fought for years, I can't wait to get inside the ring and show what I got, "De La Hoya said of meeting the undefeated Gonzalez at the Thomas & Mack Arena in Las Vegas in his first bout since destroying the Mexican challenger's legendary countryman Julio Cesar Chavez in four rounds on June 7.
"I just missed being in the spotlight," said De La Hoya, 22-0, in a teleconference call from his training camp in Big Bear, California, Wednesday.
De La Hoya was scheduled to fight Gonzalez in October, but when he was diagnosed with tendinitis in his left shoulder in September, the fight was pushed back.
Seven weeks of therapy and two months of training have him back in perfect condition and ready for anything the WBC's No. 1 rated contender will throw at him, said the 23-year-old De La Hoya.

"If he wants to mix it up or box, I'm there for him," De La Hoya said of Gonzalez,41-0. "I know he is going to be well conditioned and hungry, and he has said he wants to bring the title back to Mexican because that's where he says it belongs."
A victory by De La Hoya and one by Pernell Whitaker on Jan 24 in Atlantic City over Cuban defector Diobelis Hurtado, would thrust the two superstars into a showdown sometime in April.
Everybody is aching for that fight said De La Hoya.
"That's what boxing needs, big fights," De La Hoya. "To bring boxing back to where it belongs, it's going to take big fights and I want to do that."
